maria: FYI pushed a small terraform change in infra/vpc — plan now shows ~10 subnets to be replaced. I only reordered the var.subnets list. Did I break state mapping? anyone else see this? :eyes:

lee: Can you paste the resource block and the var shape? Did you switch count <-> for_each?

maria: snippet: ```hcl
variable "subnets" {
  type = list(object({ name = string, cidr = string }))
}

resource "aws_subnet" "app" {
  for_each = { for s in var.subnets : s.name => s }
  cidr_block = each.value.cidr
  tags = { Name = each.value.name }
}
```
I didn't touch the resource, only reordered the list in the var.

rahul: If you used for_each mapping by name it should be stable. But if state was created with count or an index-based key then reordering will change mapping. Run: `terraform state list | grep aws_subnet.app` and `terraform state show 'aws_subnet.app["subnet-name"]'` to inspect.

maria: ran `terraform state list | wc -l` -> 10. state shows keys like `aws_subnet.app["subnet-1"]` etc. In plan output it's replacing `aws_subnet.app["subnet-3"]` -> recreate, etc. Looks like names in var shifted (subnet-3 is now at a different index).

lee: Did the var elements change their `name` value or only order? If `name` changed then key changes. If only order, keys should be stable when for_each uses `s.name`. Show the tfvars before/after.

maria: here's the diff I pushed: <https://example.com/repo/commit/abcd1234> — old list was [subnet-a, subnet-b, subnet-c, ...], new list is reordered. No renames.

rahul: Another possibility: earlier code might have constructed the for_each map differently, e.g. `for_each = toset(var.subnets)` or `zipmap(range(length(var.subnets)), var.subnets)` which is order-sensitive. Confirm the exact expression in your branch and in the state history.

lee: Quick debug: run `terraform plan -refresh=false` to see planned actions without refresh. If refresh is changing attributes (tags, external network allocations) that could also trigger replacements. Also check `terraform providers lockfile` for provider bumps.

maria: running now... still shows replaces. env: `terraform 1.6.0`, aws provider `~> 4.50`. No provider upgrade in this commit.

rahul: If the for_each key was computed from position (eg index-derived name) reordering will naturally remap. If you want stable identity across reorder, use an explicit map keyed by a stable identifier (like the subnet name) in your tfvars or the mapping expression.

maria: it already is using the `s.name => s` map. Strange.

deploy-bot: Reminder: scheduled apply tonight 23:00 UTC if plan looks ok. :robot_face: 

lee: Another quick script to help debug mapping mismatches: paste old/new var arrays then run a small check locally to find moved entries. Example: ```bash
python - <<'PY'
old = ["subnet-a", "subnet-b", "subnet-c"]
new = ["subnet-b", "subnet-c", "subnet-a"]
for name in new:
    print(name, '->', old.index(name) if name in old else 'new')
PY
```

rahul: Workaround if you need a fast fix: `terraform state mv` to remap keys from old to new names: `terraform state mv 'aws_subnet.app["subnet-a"]' 'aws_subnet.app["subnet-a"]'` (adjust as needed). Do that only for moved-but-not-renamed entries.

maria: ok trying `terraform state mv` for the two that moved. After mv plan shows only 2 replaces down from 10. nice. :tada:

lee: Long-term: either enforce deterministic ordering in the tfvars (store as map keyed by name) or add a short CI check that flags reorders that would cause mass replacements. Also document that `for_each` keys must be stable.

maria: thanks all. I'll finish the state mv and hold the apply until tomorrow morning to eyeball. cc @oncall

ops-bot: @oncall paging — manual hold requested for infra apply by maria.

maria: leaving a quick runbook in the PR with the `terraform state mv` steps and a note about stable keys and why reordering is dangerous.

rahul: one more note — `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [tags] }` might hide tag churn, but don't use it to paper over identity issues.

lee: also add a line in the PR description: `If you reorder lists, run the mapping check script and consider using maps instead of lists.`

maria: will do. thanks :heart:
